author: Antigravity Biomedical Engineering Team
core_hypothesis: Unified Hierarchical Multi-Stream Consensus Operator (HMSCO v24): We hypothesize that multi-stream electrophysiological evidence in disorders of consciousness is governed by a unified multi-stream architecture: (1) Soft-maximum nonlinear pooling via an Lp power-mean operator (p in [1.4, 1.8]), which preserves surviving intact pathways; (2) Continuous Fisher Discriminant Ratio (FDR) quality weighting (alpha in [0.0, 0.10]), which adaptively prioritizes the higher-SNR sensory pathway; (3) Analytical collinearity-gated scalar shrinkage (r0 = 0.88), which prevents redundant variance explosion in highly collinear channels; and (4) Adaptive Reference/Noise Stream Regularization (lambda in [0.0, 0.1, 0.2]), where the degree of spontaneous non-neural baseline suppression is jointly selected inside patient-isolated inner cross-validation folds. Under strictly fair and identical feature inputs across cohorts, we hypothesize that the inner-CV tuned HMSCO (hmsco_v24_tuned) will simultaneously (a) outperform simple linear summation by a significant margin across all cohorts, (b) strictly exceed the v21 strong baseline (0.8280) on Binder under pure inner-CV selection without manual hyperparameter fixing, and (c) resolve multi-stream dilution across distinct recording paradigms.
